title: となりのトトロ (Tonari no Totoro — My Neighbor Totoro)
description:
The ending theme of Studio Ghibli's beloved 1988 film となりのトトロ (My Neighbor Totoro), directed by Hayao Miyazaki. Lyrics by 宮崎駿 (Hayao Miyazaki), music and arrangement by 久石譲 (Joe Hisaishi), performed by 井上あずみ (Inoue Azumi) with the Suginami Children's Choir. The song describes the magical, once-in-a-childhood experience of encountering the forest spirit Totoro — leaving secret acorns in alleyways, sheltering under a giant umbrella at a rainy bus stop, and hearing an ocarina on a moonlit night. It captures the essence of Miyazaki's belief that the natural world is full of wonder visible only to children.

For learners: Ideal N5 listening material. The vocabulary is gentle and poetic. Key words: こっそり (secretly, stealthily), 小路 (alleyway, small path), 木の実 (nuts, acorns), 秘密 (secret), 冒険 (adventure), むかし (long ago, once upon a time), 月夜 (moonlit night), オカリナ (ocarina), 不思議 (mysterious, wonderful), 出会い (encounter, meeting), しあわせ (happiness). The recurring 'トトロ トトロ' refrain makes it easy to follow along from first listen.
